name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

areaKm2.note: World Bank land area 241,930 km2; total area incl. inland water ~242,500 km2 (mid); polygon world_1960 United Kingdom computes to ~219,000 km2 on the sphere (coarse coastline), so the polygon is not used.

population.note: OWID population 1982 = 56,292,761 (mid); COW NMC v7 tpop 1982 = 56,318k (high); MB 1982-83 gives 55,965,000 (low). UK only; Falkland Islanders (~1,800) excluded.

activePersonnel.note: IISS Military Balance 1981-1982 (data as at 1 July 1981), Britain entry, as transcribed at the cited page: total armed forces 343,646 (Army 176,248, Navy incl. FAA and RM 74,687, RAF 92,701); IISS Military Balance 1982-1983 (data as at July 1982, after the war), Britain entry (http://samlib.ru/t/temezhnikow_e_a/mb1982.shtml): 327,600. COW NMC v7 milper 1982 = 335k, used as mid for April 1982.

trainedReserves.note: IISS Military Balance 1981-1982 (data as at 1 July 1981), Britain entry, as transcribed at the cited page: Army 137,000 regular reserves + 69,500 TA + 7,500 UDR; Navy/RM 25,000 regular + 9,000 volunteer; RAF 28,000 regular + ~400 volunteer = ~276,400. Low allows for regular reservists with lapsed training.

supportPersonnel.note: Everything outside the infantry P roles: Navy and RAF entirely (less the 3 RM commandos), plus Army armour, artillery, engineers, signals, aviation, logistics and staffs = active ~335,000 minus ~39,000 infantry (reconstruction from the MB order of battle).

mobilizationRatio.note: Analogue: united-kingdom-1939 snapshot (WWII peak ~5.1M in uniform of ~48M = 0.106, Harrison 1998), scaled down for a volunteer force without conscription since 1960.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1981-1982 (data as at 1 July 1981), Britain entry, as transcribed at the cited page: BAOR 4 armd div with ~12-14 mechanised (FV 432) battalions at ~650 each. MB gives 48 inf bn in total without splitting mechanised from light; split is a reconstruction from the BAOR order of battle.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: SLR 7.62 mm, GPMG, Milan, FV 432 APC (1960s); MCV-80 on order

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75-1.0. Evidence: long-service volunteers, BATUS, Northern Ireland tours

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1981-1982 (data as at 1 July 1981), Britain entry, as transcribed at the cited page: remaining ~35 inf bn + 5 Gurkha bn + 3 para bn + SAS + 3 RM commandos (RM 7,899 total) at ~600-750 each. In the Falklands the British land force peaked at 13,000 (Middlebrook pp. 86-88 via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Falklands_War), built on 3 Commando Bde and 5 Infantry Bde.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: light role, SLR/GPMG/Milan, few night sights; outranged by some Argentine artillery

training.note: Rubric row: training 1.0 (elite long-service professionals). Evidence: Paras, Royal Marines, Gurkhas and SAS won night battles against conscripts in June 1982

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1981-1982 (data as at 1 July 1981), Britain entry, as transcribed at the cited page: 100 105 mm light guns/pack howitzers, 93 FH-70, 50 M-109, 31 M-107, 16 M-110 = 290 plus an unstated number of FV 433 Abbot (~150, educated estimate: ~8 regiments). Lance under missiles; mortars excluded.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: L-118 light gun excellent in the Falklands; Abbot obsolescent

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: professional Royal Artillery

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1981-1982 (data as at 1 July 1981), Britain entry, as transcribed at the cited page: 900 Chieftain MBT (60 in reserve) + 271 FV 101 Scorpion light tanks. Mid = 840 active Chieftain + 271 Scorpion; high adds the 60 in reserve; low = Chieftain only. 2 troops of Scorpion/Scimitar (Blues and Royals) went to the Falklands.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Chieftain 120 mm gun and thick cast armour but unreliable L60 engine; Challenger on order (243)

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: professional BAOR crews

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1981-1982 (data as at 1 July 1981), Britain entry, as transcribed at the cited page: APC 2,338 FV 432 + 600 FV 603 Saracen + 60 FV 103 Spartan = 2,998; high adds 243 Saladin, 290 Scimitar, ~200 Fox recce (Ferret scout cars excluded). MB 1982-83 adds 500 FV 1611 Humber Pig.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: 1960s FV 432 and 1950s Saracen; no IFV yet

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: professional mechanised infantry

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1981-1982 (data as at 1 July 1981), Britain entry, as transcribed at the cited page: 2 sqn with 24 Lightning (24 more in reserve, high) + 7 sqn with 88 Phantom + 24 Phantom FGR-2 OCU + 20 Sea Harrier FRS-1 = 156. For the Falklands the task force sailed with 28 Sea Harriers (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Falklands_War).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Phantom FGR-2/FG-1 capable; Lightning 1960s; Sea Harrier subsonic but with AIM-9L supplied for the war

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75-1.0. Evidence: Sea Harrier pilots scored ~20 air-to-air kills without air-to-air loss in 1982

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1981-1982 (data as at 1 July 1981), Britain entry, as transcribed at the cited page: front line 48 Vulcan B-2 (being disbanded from 1981, ~3 sqn left by April 1982) + 60 Buccaneer + 72 Jaguar + 48 Harrier GR-3 = 228 (low); with OCU aircraft (9 Vulcan, 14 Buccaneer, 26 Jaguar, 27 Harrier, 39 Tornado TTTE) = 343 (high). Mid allows for the Vulcan drawdown.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Jaguar/Buccaneer capable low-level strike; Tornado GR-1 just entering squadron service; Vulcan 1950s design (Black Buck raids)

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75-1.0. Evidence: Black Buck 12,000 km tanker-supported raids; Harrier GR-3 close support from Hermes

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1981-1982 (data as at 1 July 1981), Britain entry, as transcribed at the cited page: Army ~315 (100 Scout, 7 Alouette II, 20 Sioux, 158 Gazelle, 30 Lynx); FAA ~245 (Sea King, Lynx, Wasp, Wessex incl. training); RM 18; RAF ~110 (Wessex, Puma, Whirlwind, Sea King, Chinook). Summed from the MB squadron lists, grade C.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Sea King and Lynx modern; Wessex, Wasp, Scout and Whirlwind 1950s-60s; 3 of 4 Chinooks lost on Atlantic Conveyor

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75-1.0. Evidence: night and bad-weather flying in the Falklands

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1981-1982 (data as at 1 July 1981), Britain entry, as transcribed at the cited page: 62 major surface combat vessels = 2 ASW carriers (Invincible, Hermes) + 14 GW destroyers (6 County, 1 Type 82, 7 Type 42) + 46 frigates; 1 destroyer and 9 frigates in refit or reserve (low). Task force 1982: 43 RN vessels, 22 RFA, 62 merchant ships (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Falklands_War).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Sea Dart and Sea Wolf, but no airborne early warning, no CIWS, many 1960s hulls; 2 Type 42 and 2 Type 21 lost to air attack

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75-1.0. Evidence: Flag Officer Sea Training work-ups; damage control and ASW proficiency

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1981-1982 (data as at 1 July 1981), Britain entry, as transcribed at the cited page: 38 minesweepers/minehunters + 25 patrol craft + 2 LPD (Fearless, Intrepid) + 6 landing ships (RFA LSL) = 71. Hovercraft excluded.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: mostly 1950s Ton class MCM; Hunt class entering service

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: professional RN; some Ton class with reserves

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1981-1982 (data as at 1 July 1981), Britain entry, as transcribed at the cited page: 4 Resolution SSBN + 12 SSN (6 Swiftsure, 3 Churchill, 2 Valiant, 1 Dreadnought) + 16 diesel (13 Oberon, 3 Porpoise) = 32; 1 SSBN, 3 SSN and 4 SS in refit/reserve (low). HMS Conqueror sank ARA General Belgrano on 2 May 1982.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75-1.0. Evidence: SSN with Mk 8/Mk 24 Tigerfish torpedoes (Tigerfish unreliable)

training.note: Rubric row: training 1.0. Evidence: Perisher course; SSN deployment kept the Argentine surface fleet in port after 2 May

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1981-1982 (data as at 1 July 1981), Britain entry, as transcribed at the cited page: 1 missile regiment with 12 Lance SSM launchers. Polaris SLBM tubes counted with the SSBN under submarines (project convention).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Lance 120 km SSM

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: professional Royal Artillery

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1981-1982 (data as at 1 July 1981), Britain entry, as transcribed at the cited page: Army 3 AD regt with 108 Rapier/Blindfire (MB 1982-83: each regt of 3 btys with 12 fire units = 9 btys); RAF Regiment 6 Rapier sqn; RAF 2 Bloodhound 2 sqn (~4 flights). ~19 battery equivalents. Blowpipe MANPADS excluded.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: Rapier capable but suffered teething problems at San Carlos; no medium/long-range modern Army SAM

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: professional crews

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.75 (trained staff system, proven commanders). Evidence: improvised 12,800 km joint campaign planned and launched within days (task force sailed 5 April 1982); Northwood command of a joint task force

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.75-1.0. Evidence: regimental system; Paras, RM and Guards fought on after heavy losses (Goose Green, Mount Tumbledown)

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.75 (motivated). Evidence: national rally after the Argentine invasion of 2 April 1982; volunteer force with clear cause

weapons.note: Anchor: between 8 (1943) and 9 (1985). Evidence: Sea Dart, Sea Wolf, Rapier, Milan, Sidewinder AIM-9L (US-supplied), Exocet on frigates; Chieftain with laser rangefinder

armor.note: Anchor: between 8 (rolled armour) and 9 (composite). Evidence: Chieftain cast steel; Chobham composite only on order (Challenger from 1983)

ships.note: Anchor: between 8 and 9 (nuclear subs, Aegis). Evidence: 12 SSN and 4 SSBN; Type 22 with Sea Wolf; no AEW, no CIWS, Hermes 1959

fortification.note: Anchor: towards 9 (hardened shelters). Evidence: HAS at RAF Germany bases; no hardening in the South Atlantic

logistics.note: Anchor: towards 9 (containerised, airlift). Evidence: Ascension staging, Victor tankers, VC-10/C-130 airlift; 62 requisitioned merchant ships (STUFT) for the task force

communications.note: Anchor: towards 9 (satellite comms). Evidence: Skynet/SCOT satellite links on major warships, Clansman radios; Link 10/11 between ships

isr.note: Anchor: between 8 (radar) and 9 (satellites). Evidence: Nimrod MR/R-1, US satellite and SIGINT support; no carrier AEW (Sea King AEW rushed in after the war)

air.note: Anchor: between air 8 (1943) and 9 (1985). Evidence: Harrier/Sea Harrier V/STOL, Phantom, Buccaneer, Jaguar; Tornado GR-1 just entering service

cyber.note: No state computer-network attack capability before ~1985 in this project convention (anchor cyber 9 = 1990 networks).

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 (OWID CSV): United Kingdom 1982 = 20,650 (2011 int$).

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: SIPRI via World Bank: 1982 = 5.38% (wartime year, mid), 1981 = 4.98% (last peacetime, low). High: MB 1982-83 defence budget GBP 14.09 bn vs 1981 GDP GBP 235.27 bn = 6.0% (prior-year GDP, overstates).

industrialShare.note: Educated guess: World Bank industry share for the UK starts in 1990 (27.6%); 1982 was higher before the mid-1980s manufacturing decline but North Sea oil was near its peak.

foodSurplus.note: Formula: foodSurplus = 1 - agricultural share of the labour force (share of food output not eaten by the farm population; no calorie self-sufficiency adjustment). World Bank WDI Database Archives (version 1999 Apr), SL.AGR.TOTL.ZS "Labor force in agriculture (% of total)" (ILO-based) United Kingdom 1982 = 2.5%. The UK was a net food importer; that does not lower this value. Share 2.5% (range 1.5-3.5%) -> 0.975 (0.965-0.985).

annualCohort.note: World Bank SP.POP.1519.MA.5Y GBR 1982 = 8.83% of males aged 15-19; SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN GBR 1982 = 27,395,187 (https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/GBR/indicator/SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN?date=1982&format=json). 27,395,187 x 8.83% / 5 = ~484,100 males per year. audit 2026-10-30: males only, the conscript-pool convention of all other snapshots (derived:cohort-from-agegroup applied to the male term only); was 994,000 for both sexes with an assumed female share.

artillery.note: Educated guess: L-118 light gun, FH-70 (trinational).

armor.note: Educated guess: Chieftain (Shir/Khalid export line) and first Challengers at ROF Leeds.

ifv_apc.note: Educated guess: FV 432 out of production; Spartan/Scorpion family at Alvis Coventry; MCV-80 not yet in production.

aircraft_fighter.note: Educated guess: Sea Harrier at Kingston/Dunsfold (replacements ordered after the war); Tornado F-2 prototype stage.

aircraft_strike.note: Educated guess: Tornado GR-1 UK share (~50/yr in 1982-85) plus Harrier GR-3 attrition replacements.

helicopters.note: Educated guess: Westland Sea King and Lynx lines at Yeovil.

ships_major.note: Educated guess: Type 22 frigates, Type 42 destroyers and the Invincible-class carriers building in 1982.

ships_minor.note: Educated guess: Hunt class MCMV, Castle patrol vessels.

submarines.note: Educated guess: Trafalgar SSN at Vickers Barrow, ~1 per year.

air_defense.note: Educated guess: Rapier fire units in battery equivalents.

roadKm.note: Educated guess: public road network of Great Britain ~340,000 km plus Northern Ireland ~24,000 km.

railKm.note: World Bank rail lines first value 1995 = 17,001 km; British Rail route length in 1982 was somewhat higher (~17,200 km) plus NIR ~330 km. Grade C.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess: London/Tilbury, Felixstowe, Southampton, Portsmouth, Plymouth, Liverpool, Glasgow/Clyde, Rosyth, Belfast, Hull, Tees, Bristol; Ascension and Gibraltar as forward bases.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess: UK-registered fleet ~20-25M grt in 1982 (down from ~33M in 1975), x1.5 to dwt. 62 merchant ships (STUFT) were requisitioned for the task force (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Falklands_War).

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess: the Falklands land campaign operated ~80-100 km from the San Carlos beachhead, itself 12,800 km from the UK and ~6,000 km from Ascension; BAOR planned on corps depots 100-300 km behind the IGB.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess: horses and ponies in the UK, no military transport role.

nuclearWarheads.note: FAS (Kristensen and Korda) via OWID: United Kingdom 1982 = 385 warheads. Polaris A-3 (Chevaline in conversion) plus WE.177 bombs and depth charges; US-custody NATO warheads for BAOR excluded.

basesAbroad.name: Port Stanley, Falkland Islands (occupied by Argentina 2 Apr to 14 Jun 1982)

homeDefense.note: 1.2 row at home: island with sea moat, familiar terrain, population support. In the Falklands the British are the attackers (1.0); the islands are a self-governing British territory whose population supported the British.

notes: Snapshot date April 1982: Argentina invaded the Falklands on 2 April, the task force sailed on 5 April, the war ended on 14 June 1982. Order of battle from IISS Military Balance 1981-1982 (data as at 1 July 1981) with personnel cross-checked against MB 1982-1983 (July 1982) and COW; both editions read from full-text transcriptions at samlib.ru (cited URLs). Falklands figures (Falklands War article, sources Middlebrook 2012 and Freedman, Official History of the Falklands Campaign vol. 2, 2005, not fetched): land forces peaked at 13,000, 127 ships (43 RN, 22 RFA, 62 merchant), 42 initial fixed-wing aircraft (28 Sea Harrier, 14 Harrier GR-3). British losses 255 killed, 2 Type 42 destroyers, 2 Type 21 frigates, 1 LSL, Atlantic Conveyor, 10 fighters, 24 helicopters. Population convention: UK only; dependencies excluded and listed as basesAbroad. Personnel: active = regular forces; reserves (regular reserve, TA, UDR, RNR, RAuxAF) = trainedReserves. Infantry P roles reconstructed from battalion counts; all else supportPersonnel. BAOR 55,000 and Berlin 3,100, RAF Germany 10,800, Hong Kong 7,100 and Cyprus garrisons were abroad and largely stayed in place during the war. Weakest values: merchant tonnage, Abbot SP gun count, wartime production (educated guesses).
